items.title: 52263_Sonny Greer oral history interview
items.q: At that time they had a band in London named Jack Hilton... I heard this band playing... The guy said, 'That's Jack Hilton.'

ctx.x: '33. They had all the advertisement on the buses, the big two-story buses, advertised like a circus. At that time they had a band in London named Jack Hilton. He was like the Paul Whiteman that was here, so this cat he had a band, we had a couple of days before we opened in London, so I was riding somewhere and I heard this band playing and I said 'That sounds like our band.'

And the only reason I could tell the difference, it wasn't out band, when it come to individual solos, you know, it wasn't there. I said, What band is that? The guy said, 'That's Jack Hilton. The Jack Hilton.' He could imitate, had everything, note for note down, but the solos couldn't get them, because them guys played solo, how they felt. Played solo, how they felt, they played solo same number one time and another time
